title: Diabetic Emergency (Low Blood Sugar)
summary: Low blood sugar can cause confusion, sweating and odd behaviour. If they can sit up and swallow safely, give sugar. If not, call for help.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} if they cannot swallow safely or do not improve
when: Unresponsive, drowsy or unable to swallow safely
Not improving 10–15 minutes after taking sugar
You are unsure whether it is diabetes-related

steps.title: Recognise low blood sugar
steps.text: Signs include sweating, shaking, pale skin, hunger, confusion, irritability or behaviour that looks like drunkenness. Ask if they have diabetes; look for a medical ID.

steps.title: Give sugar if they can swallow
steps.text: If they are responsive and able to sit up and swallow, give glucose tablets (15–20 g), or alternatives such as fruit juice, regular (non-diet) soft drink, or sweets.

steps.title: Recheck
steps.text: If they are not improving after 10–15 minutes, give more sugar and call {EMERGENCY}. If they have a glucose meter, help them check their level.

steps.title: Once improving
steps.text: Give a snack with longer-acting carbohydrate (sandwich, biscuits) and stay with them until fully recovered.

steps.title: If they become unresponsive
steps.text: Do not give anything by mouth. Place them in the recovery position if breathing and call {EMERGENCY}. Start CPR if not breathing normally.

doNot: Do not give food or drink to someone who cannot swallow safely or is drowsy
Do not leave them alone until fully recovered

sources.body: American Heart Association and American Red Cross
